_about: Freeze-thaw pothole risk: an interpretable HEURISTIC. The weights and thresholds are starting values chosen by judgement, not fitted to data and not validated. Change them here (or point ROADSENSE_FORECAST_RULES_FILE at a copy); every prediction records the hash of the rules it used.

weights._about: Share of the score each factor can contribute. They are normalised over the factors that apply, so they need not sum to 1. A factor with no data contributes 0 and lowers data quality.

categories._about: score >= high is High, >= medium is Medium, otherwise Low. Below min_data_quality a segment is never High: it is capped at Medium and flagged 'insufficient data'.

freeze_thaw._about: A day counts as a cycle when the minimum is at or below freeze_c - margin_c and the maximum at or above freeze_c + margin_c. full_cycles is the number of cycles that scores 1.0; a potential (forecast or partly known) cycle counts potential_weight of a confirmed one.

moisture._about: A wet day has at least precip_min_mm of precipitation, any snowfall, a forecast precipitation chance of at least chance_min percent, or forecast precipitation. full_wet_days wet days (history and forecast together) scores 1.0.

crack_severity._about: Per sighting: class weight x severity-band multiplier x (0.5 + 0.5 x detector confidence). The worst sighting sets the base; each additional independent trip adds repeat_boost (up to max_trips).

road_class._about: OpenStreetMap highway class to exposure (traffic and heavy vehicles), 0..1. There is no traffic-count data, so class is the stand-in. An unknown class is reported as missing, not guessed.

history._about: Past crack-to-pothole development is used as a factor only when at least min_pairs segments show it, and evaluation figures are only reported once min_outcomes predictions have an observed outcome.
